blocks.title: Common pitfalls
blocks.text: A notification burst should become one bounded store commit. Blind unread increments, perpetual retention, and a full timeline sort on every event create both correctness and responsiveness failures.

blocks.title: Keeping notification bursts responsive without losing events

steps.title: 1) Batch updates
steps.text: Schedule one store commit for a burst when profiling shows per-event commits are expensive; the reducer still processes every accepted event.

steps.title: 2) Bound the DOM
steps.text: Virtualize notification rows while retaining normalized identities, cursor evidence, and the reader's anchor.

steps.title: 3) Repair gaps
steps.text: Pause cursor advancement and request a delta or coherent snapshot when sequence continuity breaks.

steps.title: 4) Measure
steps.text: Measure snapshot usefulness, interaction latency, burst commit cost, duplicate rejection, gaps, and unread corrections.

rows: Fetch a new snapshot and preserve selection by notification ID.

Ingestion does not force one render per event.

blocks.text: Use a named feed or list, meaningful notification headings, and explicit read controls. New events do not move focus or auto-scroll a reader away from the current position. Announce a grouped count or connection transition instead of each burst item, and keep retry and Load More keyboard operable.

Begin with snapshots and polling, verify unread semantics, then enable resumable streaming for a cohort. Track duplicate rejection, gaps, unread corrections, reconnect duration, render batches, anchor movement, and assistive-technology announcement volume.

Bound recent entities, received-event identity history, and rendered rows according to the snapshot and resume contract. Payload details that are no longer needed can be evicted while compact ordering and marker metadata remain. Notification text can contain personal data, so telemetry records event class, timing, and reducer outcome rather than message content. Browser storage is optional and scoped by account; signing out clears user-specific cached data before another session can read it.

Notification importance must not be inferred from arrival frequency. A quiet security event may deserve a persistent surface while a large batch of low-priority updates may collapse into one summary. Keep delivery state, read state, and presentation urgency separate so reconnects cannot replay alerts or mark unseen items as read. If the active filter excludes a new item, update the relevant count without moving the reader's anchor.

blocks.title: scalable notifications feed answer rubric
items: Must — Merge snapshot and resumable events by notification identity and contiguous sequence.
Must — Keep unread markers and removal events authoritative across reconnect and pagination.
Strong signal — Batch projection updates without dropping accepted notifications during bursts.
Strong signal — Preserve scroll anchor, focus, and restrained announcements as new items arrive.
Expert stretch — Explain bounded storage, multi-tab coordination, and catch-up after cursor expiry.
Red flag — Advancing the resume cursor past a gap or treating unread count as a client-only increment.
